name: init
description: "Set up AMBICODE in this repository: .ambicode/ folder, config.yaml, policy packs, candidate rules and learning context. Run once per project."
argument-hint: "[--auto]"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(node *skills/init/scripts/*) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs config *) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs context write*) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs route start rules*) Read Write(.ambicode/config.yaml) Write(.ambicode/policies/drafts/**) Glob Grep Agent AskUserQuestion WebSearch
---
`--auto` in `$ARGUMENTS`: never ask, skip manual and web rules. Run commands plain; never poll.

1. `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs" --task init`. Exit 2: stop, tell user. `configExisted` and not `--auto`: AskUserQuestion: refresh or abort.
2. Read `.ambicode/config.yaml`. Launch `ambicode:scout` in background (`model`/`effort`: `skills.init.scout`), prompt: "Map this repo, write the context, return your report."
3. One Glob for manifests and lockfiles (depth 2), read them, derive `ecosystem`, `commands`, `checks.<name>.{all,file}` (`{file}` placeholder). Unknown stays null. Hold them for step 4; end your turn.
4. On the scout's report: `paths`, `include`, `exclude`, and per project `packs`, picked by the scout's findings from `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" config packs --list`. One Write of `.ambicode/config.yaml` (template shape; no `rules` key). `config packs --task init` copies the named built-ins to `.ambicode/policies/`. `config validate --task init`; on errors one corrective Write.
5. Rules are packs, never config. Candidates: the scout's conventions, unless `--auto` one WebSearch of core-stack practice and one AskUserQuestion for the user's own. Draft them per `references/rules.md`, then `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" route start rules --task init` (not with `--auto`); the user applies them at its table.
6. Summary: projects, packs, checks found/missing, context files, drafts waiting, open questions. Errors: `references/outcomes.md`.
# Context format (`.ambicode/context/`)

Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens` and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).

## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
- `index.md`: the grep target for ticket words, one file, see below.

## Per-file structure
- H1 = the file's purpose, one line, unique across all files. Exactly one H1.
- H2 sections fixed per kind, in this order, each heading at most once per file. Keep an empty section's heading, omit its bullets.
  - `overview.md`: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Projects` (`- <id> - <path> - <what it is>`), `## Stack` (`- <tool>: <role>`).
  - `navigation.md`: `## How to read` (one bullet: list, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset/limit; never Read whole large files), `## Entry points` (`- <path> - <role>`), `## Where things live` (`- <thing>: <path or glob>`), `## Naming`, `## Grep patterns` (`- <what>: <pattern>`).
  - `conventions.md`: `## Code`, `## Errors`, `## Tests`, `## Imports`; one convention per bullet.
  - module notes: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Key files` (filled by `context write` from the code: `- <path> - <Name>, <Name>, ...` per source file of the module itself, files with the most exported declarations first, within the file limit; do not write it, only a bullet that repeats a generated path as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` is kept), `## Submodules` (`- <child note path> - <what that folder holds>`, only for a module that has child modules), `## Depends on`, `## Gotchas`.
- `index.md`: H1, then exactly `## features`, `## modules`, `## controllers`, `## models`, `## literals` in this order; under each, one entry per line: `<name> | aka: <word>, <word> | where: <dir or file path>, ... | ctx: <note path>, ...`. `aka` is lowercase, comma-separated: the words a ticket would use (UI titles, abbreviations with their expansion, synonyms). `ctx` paths must be files of the bundle or already written. No invented facts, each line at most 300 characters. It has its own budget of 20000 tokens (not `maxFileTokens`) and counts toward `maxTotalTokens`.
- Bullets sorted by path or name. Same repo state gives the same file.
- No hedging ("probably", "seems"), no dates, no drifting counts.
- No code bodies: code fences are refused; a signature is one line inside a bullet. Paths over prose.
- One fact in one file; point to another by relative path.

## Bundle format for `context write`
One call, bundle on stdin; each file starts with a line `=== <path relative to .ambicode/context/>`:

```
=== overview.md
# Overview of <repo>
## Purpose
- ...
=== modules/<note path from context tree>
# <directory> module
...
```

- `ambicode context write --replace` removes context files not in the bundle; without `--replace` only the named files change.
- Output is JSON `{written, removed, check: {problems}}`. Exit 1 and nothing written when `problems` is not empty (file too large, total too large, bad index.md section or line, ctx target missing, duplicate H2 in a file, duplicate H1 across files, code fence, path outside the kinds). Fix with one more call naming only the changed files.
- `ambicode context list` prints path, H1 and approximate tokens per file, indented by folder; notes more than two levels down are counted on their level-1 parent.
- `ambicode context tree [--root <dir>...]` prints the modules of the source roots at full depth (note path, directory, depth, file count, submodules); it writes nothing.

1	# Inseer PSM Frontend
2	
3	![Latest Release](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/-/badges/release.svg?key_text=latest+release)
4	![PSM API CI Status](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/badges/dev/pipeline.svg?ignore_skipped=true)
5	![Code Coverage](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/badges/main/coverage.svg?job=unit_test&min_acceptable=76&min_good=90)
6	
7	Originally adapted from https://www.maximegris.fr/angular-electron_ we have since removed the electron component.
8	
9	- [Angular v19](https://v19.angular.dev/overview)
10	- [Latest Node.js (LTS)](https://nodejs.org/en/download)
11	
12	<!-- TODO: Add more context to this statement, e.g. a link to the old monorepo? -->
13	<!-- This repo has been separated from the monolithic repository MVP that we were using. -->
14	
15	## **Running**
16	
17	- Install [Latest Node.js (LTS)](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 
18	  - It is recommended you use NVM
19	- Clone repository and open its path in your terminal
20	- Run `npm install` to install dependencies
21	- Run `npm run web:local` (listens on port 4200, and tries to connect to the local backend), `npm run web:dev` (Listens on port 4200, tries to connect to dev server api2.vision.dev) or `npm run web:dev-remote` (same as `npm run web:dev` but wih enabled angular optimization)
22	
23	The application's entry point is `main.ts`. The app runs an Angular App (http://localhost:4200).
24	
25	### Debugging API Integrations
26	
27	- [Inseer API](https://gitlab.com/inseer/inseer-api)
28	- [Processing API](https://gitlab.com/inseer/backend/inseer_ml_pipeline)
29	  - `cd src/ProcessingAPI`
30	
31	Run this app and the listed APIs in parallel, according to their READMEs.
32	
33	## Deployments
34	
35	The application is deployed via CI/CD. Upon pushing to `main`, or `dev` build scripts are run and then artifacts are uploaded to S3. 
36	These are then automatically deployed to our dev and prod servers using codeDeploy.
37	
38	With each release, the version number must be updated for the end users' visibility.
39	
40	### Before Merging to `dev`

content.content:
./eval-replay
---
name: scout
description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---
You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Budget: about 11 tool calls. Follow this recipe exactly.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only with offset/limit <= 40 and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names; at most 2 such reads. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language translation catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60, at most 3 reads) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms. Never read generated, vendored, lock or build files.
5. Write ALL context in ONE call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --replace <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec, including `index.md`. If the JSON `check.problems` is not empty, fix it with one more call (changed files only, no `--replace`). Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

Write `## Key files` as an empty heading: `context write` fills it from the code. To describe a file, repeat its bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>`, so a reader goes down one level at a time. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

`index.md` is the navigator's grep target; the spec has its line format. Write `## features` (product capabilities named by screens, wizards, reports, dialogs), `## modules` (one line per module note), `## controllers` (components, services, guards, routes that carry behaviour), `## models` (types, enums, form shapes, state), `## literals` (UI strings and constants). Build `aka` from the user-visible text you read and the names in your notes, expanding every abbreviation; leave out what you did not see.

Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is only for the three commands above.

Final message (returned to the caller, not written to disk), compact:
- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).
# Context format (`.ambicode/context/`)

Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens` and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).

## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
- `index.md`: the grep target for ticket words, one file, see below.

## Per-file structure
- H1 = the file's purpose, one line, unique across all files. Exactly one H1.
- H2 sections fixed per kind, in this order, each heading at most once per file. Keep an empty section's heading, omit its bullets.
  - `overview.md`: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Projects` (`- <id> - <path> - <what it is>`), `## Stack` (`- <tool>: <role>`).
  - `navigation.md`: `## How to read` (one bullet: list, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset/limit; never Read whole large files), `## Entry points` (`- <path> - <role>`), `## Where things live` (`- <thing>: <path or glob>`), `## Naming`, `## Grep patterns` (`- <what>: <pattern>`).
  - `conventions.md`: `## Code`, `## Errors`, `## Tests`, `## Imports`; one convention per bullet.
  - module notes: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Key files` (filled by `context write` from the code: `- <path> - <Name>, <Name>, ...` per source file of the module itself, files with the most exported declarations first, within the file limit; do not write it, only a bullet that repeats a generated path as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` is kept), `## Submodules` (`- <child note path> - <what that folder holds>`, only for a module that has child modules), `## Depends on`, `## Gotchas`.
- `index.md`: H1, then exactly `## features`, `## modules`, `## controllers`, `## models`, `## literals` in this order; under each, one entry per line: `<name> | aka: <word>, <word> | where: <dir or file path>, ... | ctx: <note path>, ...`. `aka` is lowercase, comma-separated: the words a ticket would use (UI titles, abbreviations with their expansion, synonyms). `ctx` paths must be files of the bundle or already written. No invented facts, each line at most 300 characters. It has its own budget of 20000 tokens (not `maxFileTokens`) and counts toward `maxTotalTokens`.
- Bullets sorted by path or name. Same repo state gives the same file.
- No hedging ("probably", "seems"), no dates, no drifting counts.
- No code bodies: code fences are refused; a signature is one line inside a bullet. Paths over prose.
- One fact in one file; point to another by relative path.

## Bundle format for `context write`
One call, bundle on stdin; each file starts with a line `=== <path relative to .ambicode/context/>`:

```
=== overview.md
# Overview of <repo>
## Purpose
- ...
=== modules/<note path from context tree>
# <directory> module
...
```

- `ambicode context write --replace` removes context files not in the bundle; without `--replace` only the named files change.
- Output is JSON `{written, removed, check: {problems}}`. Exit 1 and nothing written when `problems` is not empty (file too large, total too large, bad index.md section or line, ctx target missing, duplicate H2 in a file, duplicate H1 across files, code fence, path outside the kinds). Fix with one more call naming only the changed files.
- `ambicode context list` prints path, H1 and approximate tokens per file, indented by folder; notes more than two levels down are counted on their level-1 parent.
- `ambicode context tree [--root <dir>...]` prints the modules of the source roots at full depth (note path, directory, depth, file count, submodules); it writes nothing.
---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: sonnet
---
You locate the files a change would need to touch, without editing anything. Budget: about 14 tool calls. Follow the steps in order.

1. Read `.ambicode/navigator/features.md` if it exists (Read, whole file). `# Index` lists directories as `<dir> (<files>) | <child dirs>`; `# Learned` lines are `## <feature> | terms: ... | files: ... | deps: ... | models: ...`. FIRST match the ticket's named modules and terms against Index directory names and Learned entries, then Grep/Glob inside the matched directories before any repo-wide grep. Take matching Learned `files` and `deps` as first candidates. Example: ticket "fix the Foo wizard", index line `app/modules/foo (40) | wizard, score-card` -> Glob `app/modules/foo/**/wizard*`.
2. Turn the prompt into 3 to 6 search words: the nouns it uses, their code spellings (camelCase, kebab-case, singular and plural) and the synonyms from the matching features' `terms`. Grep (files-with-matches) and Glob for them. Ignore words that match more than about 40 files.
3. Run on the best 6 to 10 candidates, in ONE call, with repository-relative paths:
   `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure <path> <path> ...`
   It prints each file's exports, the repo files it imports with the names imported, and external packages. Bash is only for this command. Output is capped: when it ends with `N more lines; pass fewer paths`, re-run it on the paths it did not show (batches of fewer paths) before filtering.
4. One hop: run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure --hop <the same paths>` once. It lists files the set imports but does not contain, with the imported names. Follow a dependency only when its imported names serve the task.
5. Filter. Keep a file only if the task changes it, or if a file you keep calls a name it declares and the change needs that name. Read a file (Read, limit 60) only when its role is unclear. Drop files that merely matched a word. Before the final filter, Glob the directory of each kept component or family, and list its siblings (per-variant copies, the template and style files beside a `.ts` component) when the change reaches them. Example: keeping `x/card.component.ts` for a label change, Glob `x/card.component.*` and keep `card.component.html` if the label is in it.

You find the files a change would need to change or read, without editing anything. Work from the ticket's words, not its product area. Budget: about 12 tool calls; stop when lookups add nothing.

1. Before any tool call, write the ticket breakdown in your reply, from the ticket text alone:
   - features: product capabilities the ticket names (what the user sees or does), in ticket order.
   - modules: code areas or folders those features likely live in.
   - controllers: the pieces that handle the behaviour: screens, components, dialogs, handlers, services, routes, guards.
   - models: data shapes: types, enums, DTOs, state, constants, schemas.
   - literals: exact strings, keys, selectors, constants. For a new one, the old value it replaces, if the ticket says so.
   Fold rules and constraints into the most fitting category, not a separate section. This is the search plan.
2. The only map is the index `.ambicode/context/index.md`. Sections: features, modules, controllers, models, literals. Line: `name | aka: ... | where: <paths> | ctx: <notes>`. Never Read it whole and never Glob or Grep the source tree to discover places. Grep the index (one call per few words, `-i`, with line output) for the breakdown words, specific first (a rare name, a literal, a compound term). A generic word only together with a specific one. Try the code spelling too (kebab, camel, singular, plural).
3. For each matched line, Read the notes in `ctx:` (under `.ambicode/context/`). Keep each `where:` place by default; drop a file or directory only when you are sure it does not fit the ticket (the note or structure clearly shows it is about something else). Doubt means keep.
4. If the notes do not settle it, look at the source by structure only, one call from the repo root, at most 8 files: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure <file> <file> ...`. It takes tracked file paths, not directories, and prints per file the declared names (with line numbers) and the repo files it imports. No bodies. On `N more lines; pass fewer paths`, re-run on the paths not shown. Then apply the keep rule.
5. One step from an anchor, no more. If a kept file imports something relevant to the ticket and not yet considered, check it the same way: its index line and note if it has one, else structure. Do not follow imports of that file further, and do not start from a file that is not an index anchor or a direct import of one.
6. List every kept place (the keep rule of step 3 applies to the whole list). Never list companion files: style sheets, markup templates, tests, mocks, stories (e.g. .scss, .css, .html, *.spec.*, *.test.*, *.mock.*, *.stories.*). List the logic file of that component or module instead. A directory with a trailing `/` is allowed when the whole folder is the unit of change.
7. If the index is missing, or no breakdown word matches a line, say so in one line, then fall back briefly: list tracked paths filtered by the breakdown words (`git ls-files | grep -iE 'words'`), Grep exact names in content (files mode) inside the found folders, and keep what the change touches. Update Input Type Labels for REBA, RULA, and EST Wizard + Effort Details

**Summary:**  
Update input type labeling for **REBA**, **RULA**, and **EST** so that wizard fields, Scorecard Effort Details, shorthand indicators, and export resources use the new input type taxonomy: **AI**, **AI (overridden)**, **Calculated**, and **Manual**.

**Description:**  
As an ergonomist or safety professional completing or reviewing REBA, RULA, or EST assessments, I want all wizard and effort detail inputs to use consistent input type labels so that I can clearly understand whether a value was AI-generated, manually entered, calculated, or AI-generated and manually corrected.

This ticket applies to:

* **REBA:** Modal Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* **RULA:** Modal Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* **EST:** Single-Page Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* Export resources that display input type labels, including Share Report and other report/export outputs

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* REBA modal wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* RULA modal wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* EST single-page wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* REBA, RULA, and EST display “AI (overridden)” when a user manually edits an AI-generated value.
* Restore AI behavior reverts overridden AI values back to the original AI-generated value and changes the label back to “AI.”
* Manual values remain labeled as “Manual.”
* Calculated or derived values display as “Calculated” where applicable.
* REBA and RULA shorthand indicators and badges display “AI” for machine-generated inputs and “ai(o)” for AI-originated overridden values where shorthand is used.
* REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details display the updated input type taxonomy in the Input Type column.
* Export resources that include input type labels, including Share Report and other report/export outputs, use the same updated taxonomy.
* No user-facing wizard, Effort Details, shorthand indicator, or export label for these score types displays “Vision” or “CV.”
* All labels and shorthand indicators use the approved translation keys.

# Navigator search behaviour: bare vs plugin traces

Offline analysis of kept traces. No product code touched, no paid runs.

## Data and method

- Traces: `evals/cases/results/traces/{plugin,bare}/<run>/fe-vs-<id>-investigate-1.jsonl`. Passes by start time: plugin pass 1 = 15:43-15:49, pass 2 = 16:27-16:34, pass 3 = 17:06-17:31 (all 2026-10-17); bare pass 1 = 15:50-15:55, pass 2 = 16:35-16:41. 30 plugin runs and 20 bare runs over the 10 cases. A second early plugin run of case 438 (15:28-15:56) exists and is ignored.
- Truth = `relevant` list in each case's `truth.json` (navigation files: no i18n dirs, specs, mocks, fixtures). Score = recall over the ```files block of the main session's last message (what the grader reads).
- "Surfaced" = the truth path or its basename appears in a Grep/Glob/Bash output. Read results are not counted (they show contents, not paths). `ls`/`cd`-relative output shows bare names, so surfacing by listing is slightly undercounted for bare. Parsing scripts were throwaway (`/tmp/trn/*.mjs`), not kept in the repo.
- Re-checked numbers against `evals/history.md`: bare pass 2 mean recall 0.381, plugin pass 3 0.370. Same.

## Why bare beat plugin on 6141, 438, 3571 and what decided 5967, 6292, 5164

6141 (56 truth, bare b2 31 hits vs plugin 1/3/6; bare b1 only 5):
- The decisive move was breadth by directory, not search. Bare b2 listed every tracked path whose name carries a ticket module word (150 lines) and returned whole families of components from the listing: 129 files, 31 truth. Plugin ran only content greps for the label identifiers (12 to 22 greps, first 2 grep results 0 truth in 5 of 5 runs) and returned 14 to 37 files named by content hits.
- Plugin p3 saw 25 truth files in one grep and 14 in a count-mode grep, then answered 37 files with 6 truth. The final filter removed the family.
- One run is luck: bare b1 (same prompt, same arm) returned 70 files with 5 truth. The breadth win needs the listing to name the families; b1 never listed them.

438 (3 truth, bare 3/3 twice, plugin 3,3,2):
- Bare's recipe: one grep on the verbatim label (2 of 3 surfaced), one glob on `*employee*`, three whole-file reads, one reverse grep. Final: 11 to 12 files with the dialog the component opens, the facade, the scss and module.
- Plugin p3 saw the same files and dropped the dialog. The cause is the keep rule, not search.

3571 (49 truth, bare 17 and 22 vs plugin 9, 12, 16):
- Both arms surfaced about the same (23 truth in the `[Vv]iewer` grep result). Bare kept 17 to 22 files of the 23, plugin 9 to 16. Plugin removed files that "merely matched a word" (module files, employee-notes, edit-wizard-section-button, 6 to 8 files). Bare started from the tracked-file listing, which already put 15 truth files in view in its first call.

5164 (plugin wins, 3/3/3 vs bare 3/0):
- Plugin globbed the folder named by a ticket term (`ge-adv/{components/wizard/*,services/*,...}`) as its second call in 3 of 3 runs, then ran structure on the shared service that imports it. Bare reached the same files by listing and `cat`, but pass 2 returned paths relative to the wrong root.
- It is a path-format failure on bare's side, not a search advantage. Plugin's gain here is real only in that its structure output prints repo-relative paths.

5967 and 6292: no consistent winner. Both are fan-out tickets (23 and 29 truth files, nearly all consumers or variants of one thing). Every run found the one core file and the service and 3 to 4 consumers, then stopped. Family members were in view in most runs (6292 bare b2: 11 manual-inputs components seen and dropped; 5967 plugin p3: 14 truth in one count grep over the feature folder, 3 kept). No run returned the family. Hypothesis, not measured: the keep rule asks whether the task changes each member.

Budget: about 11 tool calls. Model: sonnet. Tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob.

1. Read `templates/context-format.md` once. It is the spec for every file.

5. Write everything in ONE call: `ambicode context write --task init --replace <<EOF` with `=== <path>` bundle blocks. If `check.problems` is not empty, fix with one more call.

The scout then returns project suggestions, up to 10 candidate rules, the files written and unknowns.

### What it writes (`.ambicode/context/`, gitignored)

- `overview.md`: purpose, projects, stack.
- `navigation.md`: entry points, where things live, naming, grep patterns.

- `modules/<dir>.md` or `modules/<dir>/overview.md`: one note per module. Sections: Purpose, Key files (filled by `context write` from the code, not by the scout), Submodules, Depends on, Gotchas.

Shape: one H1, then exactly five H2 sections in this order: `features`, `modules`, `controllers`, `models`, `literals`.

- modules: one line per module note.

- models: types, enums, form shapes, state.

1	---
2	name: scout
3	description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
4	tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
5	model: sonnet
6	---
7	You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Budget: about 11 tool calls. Follow this recipe exactly.
8	
9	1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
10	2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
11	3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
12	4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only with offset/limit <= 40 and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names; at most 2 such reads. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language translation catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60, at most 3 reads) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms. Never read generated, vendored, lock or build files.
13	5. Write ALL context in ONE call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --replace <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec, including `index.md`. If the JSON `check.problems` is not empty, fix it with one more call (changed files only, no `--replace`). Never use Write.
14	
15	`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.
16	
17	Write `## Key files` as an empty heading: `context write` fills it from the code. To describe a file, repeat its bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares.
18	
19	A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>`, so a reader goes down one level at a time. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.
20	
21	`index.md` is the navigator's grep target; the spec has its line format. Write `## features` (product capabilities named by screens, wizards, reports, dialogs), `## modules` (one line per module note), `## controllers` (components, services, guards, routes that carry behaviour), `## models` (types, enums, form shapes, state), `## literals` (UI strings and constants). Build `aka` from the user-visible text you read and the names in your notes, expanding every abbreviation; leave out what you did not see.
22	
23	Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is only for the three commands above.
24	
25	Final message (returned to the caller, not written to disk), compact:
26	- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
27	- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
28	- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
29	- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).

content.content:
1	# Context format (`.ambicode/context/`)
2	
3	Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
4	Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens` and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).
5	
6	## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
7	- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
8	- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
9	- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
10	- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
11	- `index.md`: the grep target for ticket words, one file, see below.
12	
13	## Per-file structure
14	- H1 = the file's purpose, one line, unique across all files. Exactly one H1.
15	- H2 sections fixed per kind, in this order, each heading at most once per file. Keep an empty section's heading, omit its bullets.
16	  - `overview.md`: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Projects` (`- <id> - <path> - <what it is>`), `## Stack` (`- <tool>: <role>`).
17	  - `navigation.md`: `## How to read` (one bullet: list, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset/limit; never Read whole large files), `## Entry points` (`- <path> - <role>`), `## Where things live` (`- <thing>: <path or glob>`), `## Naming`, `## Grep patterns` (`- <what>: <pattern>`).
18	  - `conventions.md`: `## Code`, `## Errors`, `## Tests`, `## Imports`; one convention per bullet.
19	  - module notes: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Key files` (filled by `context write` from the code: `- <path> - <Name>, <Name>, ...` per source file of the module itself, files with the most exported declarations first, within the file limit; do not write it, only a bullet that repeats a generated path as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` is kept), `## Submodules` (`- <child note path> - <what that folder holds>`, only for a module that has child modules), `## Depends on`, `## Gotchas`.
20	- `index.md`: H1, then exactly `## features`, `## modules`, `## controllers`, `## models`, `## literals` in this order; under each, one entry per line: `<name> | aka: <word>, <word> | where: <dir or file path>, ... | ctx: <note path>, ...`. `aka` is lowercase, comma-separated: the words a ticket would use (UI titles, abbreviations with their expansion, synonyms). `ctx` paths must be files of the bundle or already written. No invented facts, each line at most 300 characters. It has its own budget of 20000 tokens (not `maxFileTokens`) and counts toward `maxTotalTokens`.
21	- Bullets sorted by path or name. Same repo state gives the same file.
22	- No hedging ("probably", "seems"), no dates, no drifting counts.
23	- No code bodies: code fences are refused; a signature is one line inside a bullet. Paths over prose.
24	- One fact in one file; point to another by relative path.
25	
26	## Bundle format for `context write`
27	One call, bundle on stdin; each file starts with a line `=== <path relative to .ambicode/context/>`:
28	
29	```
30	=== overview.md
31	# Overview of <repo>
32	## Purpose
33	- ...
34	=== modules/<note path from context tree>
35	# <directory> module
36	...
37	```
38	
39	- `ambicode context write --replace` removes context files not in the bundle; without `--replace` only the named files change.
40	- Output is JSON `{written, removed, check: {problems}}`. Exit 1 and nothing written when `problems` is not empty (file too large, total too large, bad index.md section or line, ctx target missing, duplicate H2 in a file, duplicate H1 across files, code fence, path outside the kinds). Fix with one more call naming only the changed files.
41	- `ambicode context list` prints path, H1 and approximate tokens per file, indented by folder; notes more than two levels down are counted on their level-1 parent.
42	- `ambicode context tree [--root <dir>...]` prints the modules of the source roots at full depth (note path, directory, depth, file count, submodules); it writes nothing.

content.content:
# Inseer PSM Frontend

![Latest Release](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/-/badges/release.svg?key_text=latest+release)
![PSM API CI Status](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/badges/dev/pipeline.svg?ignore_skipped=true)
![Code Coverage](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/badges/main/coverage.svg?job=unit_test&min_acceptable=76&min_good=90)

Originally adapted from https://www.maximegris.fr/angular-electron_ we have since removed the electron component.

- [Angular v19](https://v19.angular.dev/overview)
- [Latest Node.js (LTS)](https://nodejs.org/en/download)

<!-- TODO: Add more context to this statement, e.g. a link to the old monorepo? -->
<!-- This repo has been separated from the monolithic repository MVP that we were using. -->

## **Running**

- Install [Latest Node.js (LTS)](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 
  - It is recommended you use NVM
- Clone repository and open its path in your terminal
- Run `npm install` to install dependencies
- Run `npm run web:local` (listens on port 4200, and tries to connect to the local backend), `npm run web:dev` (Listens on port 4200, tries to connect to dev server api2.vision.dev) or `npm run web:dev-remote` (same as `npm run web:dev` but wih enabled angular optimization)

The application's entry point is `main.ts`. The app runs an Angular App (http://localhost:4200).

### Debugging API Integrations

- [Inseer API](https://gitlab.com/inseer/inseer-api)
- [Processing API](https://gitlab.com/inseer/backend/inseer_ml_pipeline)
  - `cd src/ProcessingAPI`

Run this app and the listed APIs in parallel, according to their READMEs.

## Deployments

The application is deployed via CI/CD. Upon pushing to `main`, or `dev` build scripts are run and then artifacts are uploaded to S3. 
These are then automatically deployed to our dev and prod servers using codeDeploy.

With each release, the version number must be updated for the end users' visibility.

# Context format (`.ambicode/context/`)

Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens` and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).

## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
- `index.md`: the grep target for ticket words, one file, see below.

## Per-file structure
- H1 = the file's purpose, one line, unique across all files. Exactly one H1.
- H2 sections fixed per kind, in this order, each heading at most once per file. Keep an empty section's heading, omit its bullets.
  - `overview.md`: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Projects` (`- <id> - <path> - <what it is>`), `## Stack` (`- <tool>: <role>`).
  - `navigation.md`: `## How to read` (one bullet: list, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset/limit; never Read whole large files), `## Entry points` (`- <path> - <role>`), `## Where things live` (`- <thing>: <path or glob>`), `## Naming`, `## Grep patterns` (`- <what>: <pattern>`).
  - `conventions.md`: `## Code`, `## Errors`, `## Tests`, `## Imports`; one convention per bullet.
  - module notes: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Key files` (filled by `context write` from the code: `- <path> - <Name>, <Name>, ...` per source file of the module itself, files with the most exported declarations first, within the file limit; do not write it, only a bullet that repeats a generated path as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` is kept), `## Submodules` (`- <child note path> - <what that folder holds>`, only for a module that has child modules), `## Depends on`, `## Gotchas`.
- `index.md`: H1, then exactly `## features`, `## modules`, `## controllers`, `## models`, `## literals` in this order; under each, one entry per line: `<name> | aka: <word>, <word> | where: <dir or file path>, ... | ctx: <note path>, ...`. `aka` is lowercase, comma-separated: the words a ticket would use (UI titles, abbreviations with their expansion, synonyms). `ctx` paths must be files of the bundle or already written. No invented facts, each line at most 300 characters. It has its own budget of 20000 tokens (not `maxFileTokens`) and counts toward `maxTotalTokens`.
- Bullets sorted by path or name. Same repo state gives the same file.
- No hedging ("probably", "seems"), no dates, no drifting counts.
- No code bodies: code fences are refused; a signature is one line inside a bullet. Paths over prose.
- One fact in one file; point to another by relative path.

## Bundle format for `context write`
One call, bundle on stdin; each file starts with a line `=== <path relative to .ambicode/context/>`:

```
=== overview.md
# Overview of <repo>
## Purpose
- ...
=== modules/<note path from context tree>
# <directory> module
...
```

- `ambicode context write --replace` removes context files not in the bundle; without `--replace` only the named files change.
- Output is JSON `{written, removed, check: {problems}}`. Exit 1 and nothing written when `problems` is not empty (file too large, total too large, bad index.md section or line, ctx target missing, duplicate H2 in a file, duplicate H1 across files, code fence, path outside the kinds). Fix with one more call naming only the changed files.
- `ambicode context list` prints path, H1 and approximate tokens per file, indented by folder; notes more than two levels down are counted on their level-1 parent.
- `ambicode context tree [--root <dir>...]` prints the modules of the source roots at full depth (note path, directory, depth, file count, submodules); it writes nothing.

# Inseer PSM Frontend

![Latest Release](https://gitlab.com/inseer/front/inseer-frontend/-/badges/release.svg?key_text=latest+release)

Originally adapted from https://www.maximegris.fr/angular-electron_ we have since removed the electron component.

- [Angular v19](https://v19.angular.dev/overview)
- [Latest Node.js (LTS)](https://nodejs.org/en/download)

<!-- TODO: Add more context to this statement, e.g. a link to the old monorepo? -->
<!-- This repo has been separated from the monolithic repository MVP that we were using. -->

## **Running**

- Install [Latest Node.js (LTS)](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 
  - It is recommended you use NVM
- Clone repository and open its path in your terminal
- Run `npm install` to install dependencies
- Run `npm run web:local` (listens on port 4200, and tries to connect to the local backend), `npm run web:dev` (Listens on port 4200, tries to connect to dev server api2.vision.dev) or `npm run web:dev-remote` (same as `npm run web:dev` but wih enabled angular optimization)

The application's entry point is `main.ts`. The app runs an Angular App (http://localhost:4200).

### Debugging API Integrations

- [Inseer API](https://gitlab.com/inseer/inseer-api)
- [Processing API](https://gitlab.com/inseer/backend/inseer_ml_pipeline)
  - `cd src/ProcessingAPI`

Run this app and the listed APIs in parallel, according to their READMEs.

## Deployments

The application is deployed via CI/CD. Upon pushing to `main`, or `dev` build scripts are run and then artifacts are uploaded to S3. 
These are then automatically deployed to our dev and prod servers using codeDeploy.

With each release, the version number must be updated for the end users' visibility.

# Coding Guideline for FrontEnd

## Javasript/Typescript

### Credentials handling

When adding a new confidential credential to the code please make use of the 
GitLab's CI/CD and "process.env". In particular, you should:
 - Never hardcode credentials. Use environment variables (process.env).
 - Store secrets securely in GitLab CI/CD variables.

### Meaningful, explanatory variable and function names

Examples:
Bad => Good
let vvar => let videoVariable
ackd() => assignConditionalKeypointDependencies()

### Always use types. NEVER use any/never

Always create interfaces instead of using any/unknown.

### Break down code into smaller peaces

If you see that your function/component is growing too big, don't hesitate to move some pieces of code
to another function/component

### DRY

Do not repeat yourself.
If you see that there's some duplicated or similar by the logic peaces of code, you should move
this peace of code to helper function and make it reusable. This is preferred to avoid having lots of duplicated blocks of code

### Function parameters and returns

Always set the type for function parameters and returns.
That way you can always tell what must be passed to the function and what it will return
Also parameter list shouldn't grow too big. If you have 3 >= parameters, it is considered a good practice to use object
parameter instead and pass parameters as fields of this object instead

Example:
longFunction(param1, param2, param3, param4) => longFunction({param1, param2, param3, param4})

That way we shouldn't worry about the order of the params and we can keep them all optional if needed

### Use computed/cached getters over functions

### Don't forget to unsubscribe

When subscribing to observable, always keep in mind that you must unsubscribe from it. You can do it
on component destruction, observable expiration, etc. but it should definitely happen.
Same goes for event listeners: if you add event listener for an HTML element, you always have to 
remove **the same event listener**. That means that event name, callback and options should match.

Example:

`element.addEventListener("mousedown", handleMouseDown, true);
element.removeEventListener("mousedown", handleMouseDown, false); // Fails
element.removeEventListener("mousedown", handleMouseDown, true); // Succeeds`

For more details, please refer to: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/removeEventListener#matching_event_listeners_for_removal

### Do not import the whole library if you need only one method from it

Some libraries can be very large and heavyweight so to avoid making our final bundle
being too big we should import only what's necessary

Example:
Bad:                        Good:
import _ from "lodash"; ->  import { sortBy } from "lodash"; ->  
-----
## Guideline for Feature Flags

### Feature Flag Creation

Feature flag (FF) should have:
 - meaningful and descriptive name;
 - description, which gives detailed explanation about the feature, for which the flag is being used;
 - user list/user id with IDs of engineers involved in the development and testing of the feature.
 - "Inseer-API-Dev" environment

### Feature Flag Integration in the code

Depending on the type of feature you're implementing, you can hide it under the FF using different methods:
- If this is a new page, you should hide the route to its root using "canMatch" and "FeatureFlagGuard"
in the ...-routing.module.ts file
- If this is a code block/component hidden on the already implemented,
you should hide it using the structural directive "*appFeatureFlag" and pass the feature flag's name
- if this is some functionality, you can always use "isEnabled" method to check if your feature flag is enabled

### Continious Integration / Continious Delivery

Before starting to implement the feature, discuss with PM if FF should be created or not.
Always create FF before impementing the logic it covers

Once the feature's merge request has been merged into dev, 
you should enable it for all users on DEV (Inseer-API-Dev).

Once the feature's merge request has been merged into PROD and released,
you should enable the feature flag for the Dev team on PROD
(TO BE IMPLEMENTED: DEV TEAM USER LIST ON GITLAB) ("Inseer-API-Production").

Once the feature is approved by the QA and PM, you can enable Feature flag for all users on production 
and create a follow-up ticket for FF removal

After 1-2 months create a MR with removal of the FF from the codebase

# Inseer Frontend — Claude Code Guide

## Project at a Glance

Angular 22 enterprise SPA. Source root is `main/` (not `src/`). Application builder (`@angular/build:application`). Vitest for tests. Storybook 10. No NgRx — state is managed via custom service-based **Facade pattern** in `main/state/`. GitLab CI.

The codebase is actively migrating toward the internal Coding Style Guide. New code must comply; legacy code is being brought up incrementally. If new code styling, structure, architecture are not found in our provided guidelines for implementation refer to angular 22 standards.

---

## Commands

```bash
npm run web:local        # dev server (local env)
npm run web:dev          # dev server (dev env)
npm test                 # Vitest (no browser, no watch)
npm run lint             # ESLint
npm run format           # Prettier
npm run storybook        # Storybook dev server
npm run build:web        # production build
```

---

## Directory Layout

```
(root)
├── main/                   # source root (angular.json sourceRoot)
│   ├── assets/             # static assets, i18n JSON, fonts, images
│   ├── components/         # shared dumb UI components (legacy; migrating to main/features/)
│   ├── constants/          # app-wide constants
│   ├── directives/         # shared directives
│   ├── environments/       # per-env configs
│   ├── errors/             # custom error definitions
│   ├── features/           # cross-cutting Angular features (amplitude, feature-flags, vlm, etc.)
│   ├── guards/             # route guards
│   ├── interceptors/       # HTTP interceptors
│   ├── interfaces/         # TS interfaces (contracts; legacy; prefer main/models/)
│   ├── models/             # all data shapes, enums, DTOs — single source of truth for types
│   ├── pipes/              # shared pipes
│   ├── providers/          # injection tokens + provider functions
│   ├── router/             # routing config, route-reuse strategies
│   ├── screens/            # routable page components (feature slices live here)
│   │   └── app/            # app shell: AppComponent, routing, layout, page-not-found
│   ├── scripts/            # scripts run before Angular bootstraps
│   ├── services/           # stateless API + business services
│   ├── state/              # Facade services (global app state, one facade per domain)
│   ├── styles/             # global SCSS
│   ├── types/              # standalone TS type utilities
│   ├── utils/              # generic helpers
│   ├── validators/         # custom form validators
│   └── main.ts             # bootstrap
├── .storybook/
├── angular.json
├── eslint.config.mts
└── tsconfig.json
```

### Target Architecture (VSA — in progress)

New features should follow Vertical Slice Architecture under `main/screens/<feature>/`:
```
main/
└── features/
    └── score-types/
        └── niosh/
            ├── components/         # smart/presentational sub-components
            ├── models/             # feature-scoped types
            ├── services/           # feature-scoped services
            ├── state/              # feature-scoped facade (if not global)
            ├── mocks/              # test fakes
            └── niosh.routes.ts
```
Shared code used by ≥2 features goes in `main/features/core/` (or existing `main/components/` until migration completes).
This is based on feature needs and scope. Assess and respect the existing structure of each feature rather than trying to force the structure to match this example strictly.

---

## TypeScript Rules

## TypeScript Rules

- **No `any`** — use the narrowest type, or `unknown` + a type guard below it.
- **Always annotate return types** on class methods and standalone functions. Omit only for inline callbacks where it adds no clarity. If undefined is a valid/supported state, please explicitly specify this in typing
- **Explicit access modifiers** — always write `public`, `protected`, or `private`. Default to `private readonly`; widen only when required.
- **`type` for data shapes; `interface` for contracts** — interfaces must represent implementable contracts and use the `I`-prefix convention (`ISerializable`, `IFilterable`). DTOs, API response shapes, and local models are `type`.
- **No duplicated type annotations** — specify on the left-hand side OR as a generic parameter on the right; never both.
- **TS namespaces** — use only for large, nested domain models with repetitive patterns within a single file. Cross-file namespace merging is not supported.
- **Explicit comparisons** — avoid ambiguity in conditions passed to control flow structures:
  - Keep using implicit boolean coercion where presence of a value is meant; but be explicit if concrete value is checked, e.g. use `if (array) { ... }` to check if array exists at all; but prefer `if (array.length > 0) { ... }` to `if (array.length) { ... }`.
  - Use strict `===`/`!==` equality checks by default; use loose `==`/`!=` equality when checking for value presence and you mean both `null` and `undefined`, e.g. `value != undefined`.

```ts
// Good
private readonly report: ReportDto;
public readonly title: string = '';
protected readonly jobTitles = signal<string[] | undefined>()

// Bad
report: ReportDto;
title = '';
jobTitles = signal()
```

---

## Angular Rules

### Change Detection
- **Every component must have `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`** — no exceptions, no omission of the field.

### Signals vs. RxJS
- **Default to signals** for all component-local reactive state.
- Use `input()`, `output()`, `model()`, `viewChild()`, `viewChildren()`, `contentChild()`, `contentChildren()` — not their decorator-based counterparts (`@Input`, `@Output`, `@ViewChild`, etc.).
- Convert RxJS streams to signals as early as is readable in components via `toSignal()`.
- Avoid `RxJS → Promise → Signal` chains — use `RxJS → toSignal()` directly.
- Keep `HttpClient` calls as observables; convert at the service or facade boundary.
- Avoid excessive back-and-forth: `observable → toSignal → toObservable → toSignal` is a smell.

### Templates
- Use `@if`, `@for`, `@switch` — **not** `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `ngSwitch` (deprecated since Angular 20).
- Use `$index`, `$first`, `$last`, `$count`, `$even`, `$odd` directly inside `@for` — no extra template variables.
- Prefer `@defer` for content that is unlikely to be visible on every page load (expandable panels, heavy sub-components).

### Dependency Injection
- **Use `inject()`** globally — constructor injection is no longer used and deprecated.
- Injection tokens and provider functions live in `providers/` folders.

### Host Bindings
- Use the `host` property on `@Component`/`@Directive` for class, style, and event bindings on the host element.
- Do not use `@HostBinding` or `@HostListener`.

### Standalone & NgModules
- All new components and directives must be **standalone**.
- Use `NgModule` only to bundle a set of related standalone declarables into a single importable unit (e.g., `StepperModule` that exports `StepperComponent`, `StepComponent`, `StepContentDirective`). No non-empty `declarations` in NgModules.

### Forms
- **Reactive Forms** are the default.
- No Template-Driven Forms in application code.
- Do not use Signal Forms — still experimental and incompatible with Angular Material.

### Lazy Loading
- All routed components must be wired via `loadComponent` / `loadChildren`.
- Use `@defer` proactively for below-the-fold or conditionally-visible content.

### Promises
- Avoid using `async/await` and `firstValueFrom` unless the underlying source API is Promise-based. I.e. it's ok to use `async/await` with e.g. `localforage` which is Promise-native; it's redundant to use `await firstValueFrom(...)` to wrap a call to RxJs-based HttpClient and pass the result to writable signal - in such cases, using `toSignal` directly is quite enough.

---

## State Management (Facade Pattern)

Global state lives in `main/state/` as injectable facade services. Each facade owns one domain (e.g., `AuthFacade`, `ReportFacade`, `ScoringFacade`).

- **Facades expose signals** (or observables converted to signals at the facade boundary).
- **API services** (`main/services/`) are stateless — they make HTTP calls and return observables.
- **Facades** call API services, hold state, and expose it to components.
- Class name suffix is `Facade` (not `FacadeService`): `OrgFacade`, `UserFacade`.
- Feature-scoped state that is not global stays inside the feature folder, not in `main/state/`.

---

## File & Class Naming

| Type | File name | Class name |
|---|---|---|
| Component | `niosh-wizard.component.ts` | `NioshWizardComponent` |
| Directive | `idle-timeout.directive.ts` | `IdleTimeoutDirective` |
| Pipe | `index-as-letter.pipe.ts` | `IndexAsLetterPipe` |
| Service | `niosh-api.service.ts` | `NioshApiService` |
| Facade | `scoring.facade.ts` | `ScoringFacade` |
| Guard | `auth.guard.ts` | `AuthGuard` |
| Interceptor | `auth-cookie.interceptor.ts` | `AuthCookieInterceptor` |
| Model/DTO | `niosh.model.ts` | (types/interfaces, no class suffix) |
| i18n keys | `ge-adv-neck.i18n-keys.ts` | — |
| Test | `niosh.service.spec.ts` | — |
| Storybook | `rsi-wizard.component.stories.ts` | — |

- **kebab-case** for all file names — never PascalCase filenames.
- **No JS implementation details in suffixes** — `scoring-data.model.ts` not `scoring-data.type.ts`; never `.class.ts`, `.enum.ts`, `.interface.ts`.
- **No `app-` prefix on filenames** — `app-` is a selector prefix only.
- Feature files use **short scoping prefixes** (e.g., `est-wizard.component.ts`) to aid identification when multiple tabs are open.
- Globally shared declarables use `app-` selector prefix; feature-scoped declarables use a concise feature prefix (e.g., `est-`, `niosh-`). Update selector prefixes when a component is promoted to shared.

---

## Import Ordering

Arrange imports in three groups (blank line between each):
1. Third-party / `node_modules`
2. Workspace-remote paths (use path aliases, e.g., `components/ui/alert/alert.component`)
3. Local relative paths within the current feature folder (e.g., `../../models/score.dto`)

---

## Class Member Ordering

1. Injected dependencies (`inject()` calls at field declaration)
2. Signal inputs / outputs / models
3. Other fields and accessors (getters/setters)
4. Constructor (if needed — rare with `inject()`)
5. Angular lifecycle hooks (`ngOnInit`, `ngOnDestroy`, etc.)
6. Public methods
7. Private methods

Co-locate tightly related members (a private field with its getter/setter; an interface implementation section wrapped in `// #region`).

---

## Testing (Vitest)

- Test files: `*.spec.ts`, co-located with the file under test.
- Runner: `npm test` (Vitest via `@analogjs/vitest-angular`, no browser, no watch in CI).
- Mocks live in a `mocks/` folder within the feature.
- Write unit tests for services, facades, pipes, and utils. Write component tests for non-trivial component logic.
- **Specs are not type-checked by `npm test`** — Vitest transpiles via esbuild and skips type checking, so `tsconfig.spec.json` errors accumulate silently and no CI gate catches them. Run `npx tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit` when you need certainty.
- Avoid `array.forEach(async …)` in specs: the promises are discarded, so assertions run after fixture teardown and silently never execute. Use `for…of` with `await`.

---

## Storybook

- Story files: `*.stories.ts`, co-located with the component.
- Runner: `npm run storybook`.

---

## Linting & Formatting

- ESLint flat config (`eslint.config.mts`) — run `npm run lint` before committing.
- Prettier — run `npm run format`.
- Husky pre-commit hooks enforce both.
- Accessibility rules are partially enforced at lint time (alt-text, label associations, ARIA). Fix a11y violations — do not suppress them.
- This list is non exhaustive
---

## Key Third-Party Libraries

| Library | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `@angular/material` v22 | UI component library |
| `@ngx-translate/core` | Runtime i18n |
| `rxjs` v7 | Async streams (use selectively — prefer signals in components) |
| `@sentry/angular` | Error tracking |
| `@amplitude/analytics-browser` | Product analytics (do not call directly — use `AnalyticsFacade`) |
| `ngx-toastr` | Toast notifications (do not call directly — use notification service) |
| `d3` | Data visualization |
| `ngx-mask` | Input masking |
| `openai` / `@openai/chatkit` | AI assistant features |

---

## Active Migration Priorities (in order)

1. **OnPush everywhere** — no component may use default change detection.
2. **Standalone APIs** — no new NgModule declarations; convert existing ones opportunistically.
3. **Signal-based inputs/outputs** — replace decorator-based `@Input`/`@Output` in touched files.
4. **VSA structure** — new features under `main/screens/<feature>/` following the slice layout above.
5. **Lazy loading** — all routes via `loadComponent`/`loadChildren`; add `@defer` to heavy expandable content.
6. **Facade coverage** — areas not yet using the facade pattern should be refactored to use it.
7. **kebab-case** — legacy PascalCase filename should be refactored to kebab-case naming.

When editing a file, apply migration items 1–3 to that file if it is not already compliant. Do not refactor unrelated files as part of a focused change.

13	3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
14	4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only with offset/limit <= 40 and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language translation catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. 16	
17	`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.
18	
19	Write `## Key files` as an empty heading: `context write` fills it from the code. To describe a file, repeat its bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares.
20	
21	A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>`, so a reader goes down one level at a time. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.
22	
23	`index.md` is the navigator's grep target; the spec has its line format. Its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which feature contains which modules, controllers and models, and where one feature ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Write `## features` (product capabilities named by screens, wizards, reports, dialogs), `## modules` (one line per module note), `## controllers` (components, services, guards, routes that carry behaviour), `## models` (types, enums, form shapes, state), `## literals` (UI strings and constants). 28	- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
29	- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
30	- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.

1	---
2	name: navigator
3	description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
4	tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash

6	---
7	You locate the files a change would need to touch, without editing anything. Budget: about 14 tool calls. Follow the steps in order.
8	
9	1. Read `.ambicode/navigator/features.md` if it exists (Read, whole file). `# Index` lists directories as `<dir> (<files>) | <child dirs>`; `# Learned` lines are `## <feature> | terms: ... | files: ... | deps: ... | models: ...`. FIRST match the ticket's named modules and terms against Index directory names and Learned entries, then Grep/Glob inside the matched directories before any repo-wide grep. Take matching Learned `files` and `deps` as first candidates. Example: ticket "fix the Foo wizard", index line `app/modules/foo (40) | wizard, score-card` -> Glob `app/modules/foo/**/wizard*`.
10	2. Turn the prompt into 3 to 6 search words: the nouns it uses, their code spellings (camelCase, kebab-case, singular and plural) and the synonyms from the matching features' `terms`. Grep (files-with-matches) and Glob for them. Ignore words that match more than about 40 files.
11	3. Run on the best 6 to 10 candidates, in ONE call, with repository-relative paths:
12	   `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure <path> <path> ...`
13	   It prints each file's exports, the repo files it imports with the names imported, and external packages. Bash is only for this command. Output is capped: when it ends with `N more lines; pass fewer paths`, re-run it on the paths it did not show (batches of fewer paths) before filtering.
14	4. One hop: run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure --hop <the same paths>` once. It lists files the set imports but does not contain, with the imported names. Follow a dependency only when its imported names serve the task.

Drop files that merely matched a word. Before the final filter, Glob the directory of each kept component or family, and list its siblings (per-variant copies, the template and style files beside a `.ts` component) when the change reaches them. Example: keeping `x/card.component.ts` for a label change, Glob `x/card.component.*` and keep `card.component.html` if the label is in it.

Call `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator learn "<entry>" "<entry>"` with 1 to 3 entries in the features.md line format, one quoted argument each, from files in your final list only. `terms`: the prompt's own domain words that no existing line matched, plus the feature's real name. `deps`: from the `--hop` output. `models`: entities those files use. 1	---
2	name: navigator
3	description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
4	tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
5	model: sonnet
6	---
7	You locate the files a change would need to touch, without editing anything. Budget: about 14 tool calls. Follow the steps in order.
8	
9	1. Read `.ambicode/navigator/features.md` if it exists (Read, whole file). `# Index` lists directories as `<dir> (<files>) | <child dirs>`; `# Learned` lines are `## <feature> | terms: ... | files: ... | deps: ... | models: ...`. FIRST match the ticket's named modules and terms against Index directory names and Learned entries, then Grep/Glob inside the matched directories before any repo-wide grep. Take matching Learned `files` and `deps` as first candidates. Example: ticket "fix the Foo wizard", index line `app/modules/foo (40) | wizard, score-card` -> Glob `app/modules/foo/**/wizard*`.
10	2. Turn the prompt into 3 to 6 search words: the nouns it uses, their code spellings (camelCase, kebab-case, singular and plural) and the synonyms from the matching features' `terms`. Grep (files-with-matches) and Glob for them. Ignore words that match more than about 40 files.
11	3. Run on the best 6 to 10 candidates, in ONE call, with repository-relative paths:
12	   `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure <path> <path> ...`
13	   It prints each file's exports, the repo files it imports with the names imported, and external packages. Bash is only for this command. Output is capped: when it ends with `N more lines; pass fewer paths`, re-run it on the paths it did not show (batches of fewer paths) before filtering.
14	4. One hop: run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator structure --hop <the same paths>` once. It lists files the set imports but does not contain, with the imported names. Follow a dependency only when its imported names serve the task.
15	5. Filter. Keep a file only if the task changes it, or if a file you keep calls a name it declares and the change needs that name. Read a file (Read, limit 60) only when its role is unclear. Drop files that merely matched a word. Before the final filter, Glob the directory of each kept component or family, and list its siblings (per-variant copies, the template and style files beside a `.ts` component) when the change reaches them. Example: keeping `x/card.component.ts` for a label change, Glob `x/card.component.*` and keep `card.component.html` if the label is in it.
16	6. Learn, once the list is settled and before you write the final message. Call `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" navigator learn "<entry>" "<entry>"` with 1 to 3 entries in the features.md line format, one quoted argument each, from files in your final list only. `terms`: the prompt's own domain words that no existing line matched, plus the feature's real name. `deps`: from the `--hop` output. `models`: entities those files use. This call is required: the final message may only be written after it has run, unless every file and term of your list is already on a map line. Having an answer is not a reason to skip it. The final message below is still your whole answer; never replace it with the learn output.
17	
18	Navigator errors: `navigator-learn-invalid` (entry malformed or too long: fix the line format, shorten it, call learn again); `navigator-features-invalid`, `navigator-features-too-large`, `navigator-features-exist` (seeding the map: the file has a bad line, the index is over budget, or the file already has content; none blocks your answer, continue without the map).
19	
20	Final message, exactly this shape and nothing before it:
21	
22	```files
23	<repo-relative path>
24	<repo-relative path>
25	```
26	Why:
27	<repo-relative path> - <one line: what changes there, or which name it supplies>
28	
29	Every path in the block is an existing tracked file, one per line, no bullets, no commas. A file to create goes in `Why` as `NEW <path> - <reason>`, never in the block.
30	
31	Example. Task: "show the paid date on the invoice PDF". Words: invoice, pdf, paid, date. features.md line `## billing | terms: invoice, receipt | files: src/billing/pdf.ts | deps: shared formatting | models: invoice`. The structure output shows pdf.ts importing `formatDate` from `src/shared/format.ts` and `Invoice` from `src/billing/model.ts`. The paid date is a model field and a rendering change:
32	
33	```files
34	src/billing/pdf.ts
35	src/billing/model.ts
36	```
37	Why:
38	src/billing/pdf.ts - renders the invoice rows; add the paid date line
39	src/billing/model.ts - Invoice must expose paidAt
40	
41	Learn call for that task, when the map had no `invoice` term: `... navigator learn "## billing | terms: invoice, paid date, receipt | files: src/billing/pdf.ts,src/billing/model.ts | deps: shared formatting | models: invoice"`

You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Follow this recipe exactly.

Walk the tree breadth-first: all folders of one level before any deeper. Visit each directory at most once in the whole run: keep a running list of visited directories and move on to one not on it. Locate names and files with Grep and Glob first; read content only when search results do not settle a module's purpose.

Never read a file whole (except the format spec in step 1): only heads or ranges with a line limit. Never read styles (`.css`, `.scss`, `.less`, `.sass`), tests or specs, mocks or fixtures, stories, nor generated, vendored, lock or build files.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only as heads with limit <= 40, only non-excluded ones, and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names and search. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language translation catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms.
5. After the whole context is composed, write ALL of it in ONE call, once: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --replace <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec, including `index.md`. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: do not retry, list the problems in the final reply. Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

Write `## Key files` as an empty heading: `context write` fills it from the code. To describe a file, repeat its bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>`, so a reader can find it from the parent. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
